cases.note: The pendant driver's four motions, as it declares them.
cases.expected: {"fault":null}

cases.note: A body not commanded this way declares nothing, and nothing is wrong.
cases.expected: {"fault":null}

cases.note: A name is what a command carries, so an empty one is refused before anything else about it.
cases.expected: {"fault":{"code":"unnamed","detail":"A motion has an empty name, and a name is what a command carries.","subjects":[]}}

cases.note: The same rule one level down, naming the motion.
cases.expected: {"fault":{"code":"unnamed","detail":"Motion move_l has a parameter with an empty name.","subjects":["move_l"]}}

cases.note: Transport reads a repeat as first-wins; the file is still wrong, and this is where it is said.
cases.expected: {"fault":{"code":"duplicate_motion","detail":"Two motions are named move_l, so a command naming it is ambiguous.","subjects":["move_l"]}}

cases.note: A vendor's own word in the canonical slot names both the motion and the word.
cases.expected: {"fault":{"code":"unknown_motion","detail":"Motion move_l says it is linear_move, which is not a canonical motion. Omit the field for a motion that is none of them.","subjects":["move_l","linear_move"]}}

cases.note: A value of the wrong type declares nothing and reads as absent, as every edition's JSON layer reads an optional string it cannot use — so the list is usable and the motion has no canonical.
cases.expected: {"fault":null}

cases.note: Null is the explicit spelling of absent.
cases.expected: {"fault":null}

cases.note: Exact, as transport reads it: `HOME` is a vendor word and not the canonical motion.
cases.expected: {"fault":{"code":"unknown_motion","detail":"Motion home says it is HOME, which is not a canonical motion. Omit the field for a motion that is none of them.","subjects":["home","HOME"]}}

cases.note: Subjects are dotted, motion then parameter.
cases.expected: {"fault":{"code":"duplicate_parameter","detail":"Motion move_l lists pose twice.","subjects":["move_l.pose"]}}

cases.note: Missing `required` is read as required by transport and refused here, so the reading is never the only thing that knows.
cases.expected: {"fault":{"code":"required_undeclared","detail":"Parameter probe.depth does not say whether it is required. It is read as required, which refuses plans that omit it; declare true or false.","subjects":["probe.depth"]}}

cases.note: Null is not an answer to a yes-or-no question.
cases.expected: {"fault":{"code":"required_undeclared","detail":"Parameter probe.depth does not say whether it is required. It is read as required, which refuses plans that omit it; declare true or false.","subjects":["probe.depth"]}}

cases.note: `"true"` is a string. A typed reader refuses it rather than coercing it, in every edition.
cases.expected: {"fault":{"code":"required_undeclared","detail":"Parameter probe.depth does not say whether it is required. It is read as required, which refuses plans that omit it; declare true or false.","subjects":["probe.depth"]}}

cases.note: `1` is not `true`, which is the trap §5 records for `detects_people` and the one Python's `==` falls into.
cases.expected: {"fault":{"code":"required_undeclared","detail":"Parameter probe.depth does not say whether it is required. It is read as required, which refuses plans that omit it; declare true or false.","subjects":["probe.depth"]}}

cases.note: The reference's type is a bare number, so the null this input carries is a non-finite value the format cannot spell (corpus/README.md) — and a bound that is not finite bounds nothing.
cases.expected: {"fault":{"code":"bound_invalid","detail":"Parameter move_l.pose declares min as a value that is not a finite number.","subjects":["move_l.pose"]}}

cases.note: The same, on the other end.
cases.expected: {"fault":{"code":"bound_invalid","detail":"Parameter move_l.pose declares max as a value that is not a finite number.","subjects":["move_l.pose"]}}

cases.note: No value satisfies it, so it is refused rather than read.
cases.expected: {"fault":{"code":"bound_invalid","detail":"Parameter move_l.speed declares a minimum above its maximum, so no value satisfies it.","subjects":["move_l.speed"]}}

cases.note: Equal bounds are a range with one member, which is a legal declaration.
cases.expected: {"fault":null}

cases.note: Either bound alone is a declaration about that side only.
cases.expected: {"fault":null}

cases.note: Faults are reported in declaration order: the second motion's bad canonical is behind the first motion's repeated parameter, and an edition that checked every name before any parameter would report the other one.
cases.expected: {"fault":{"code":"duplicate_parameter","detail":"Motion move_l lists pose twice.","subjects":["move_l.pose"]}}

cases.note: The second `move_l` has a bad parameter too, and the repeat is what is reported: a motion is checked by name before anything inside it.
cases.expected: {"fault":{"code":"duplicate_motion","detail":"Two motions are named move_l, so a command naming it is ambiguous.","subjects":["move_l"]}}

cases.note: A bad canonical and a bad parameter on one motion: the canonical is reported, because it is read before the parameter list.
cases.expected: {"fault":{"code":"unknown_motion","detail":"Motion move_l says it is teleport, which is not a canonical motion. Omit the field for a motion that is none of them.","subjects":["move_l","teleport"]}}

cases.note: An undeclared requirement and an inverted range on one parameter: the requirement is reported.
cases.expected: {"fault":{"code":"required_undeclared","detail":"Parameter move_l.pose does not say whether it is required. It is read as required, which refuses plans that omit it; declare true or false.","subjects":["move_l.pose"]}}
